To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) microglial activation is a key event of neuroinflammation, 2) microglial modulation is an attractive target to treat neuroinflammatory diseases and 3) bioactive lipids are new class of modulators of microglias activity.

(i) bioactive lipids can cross the blood-brain barrier and reach the CNS; (ii) they can modulate microglia activation and/or function, depending on the context; and (iii) this modulation can be either pro-inflammatory or anti-inflammatory, depending on the lipid.
dietary lipids are potent modulators of microgila activity and can therefore have important implications for brain physiology and disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of new microglia modulating agents that may be used to prevent or ameliorate neurodegenerative diseases, and to understand how these cells contribute to the pathogenesis of such diseases.
how the immune system and nutrition can influence the brain.
the role of bioactive lipids in neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bioactive lipids, including those derived from dietary intake, are important regulators of microglia activity and hence of neuroinflammation.

the microglial system is a highly complex and dynamic network of receptors, ligands, and signaling pathways, which can be modulated by bioactive lipids, thus opening new avenues for the development of new therapeutic approaches for neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases.
bioactive lipids are a new class of neuroimmune regulators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bioactive fatty acids can be considered as novel microglia modulating agents that may be of interest for the treatment of inflammatory diseases of the CNS.
microglia are able to sense and respond to bioactive fatty acids and that these molecules are likely to be involved in neuroinflammatory processes.
the bioactive lipid field has been largely neglected for a long time, and that the time has come to consider them as new class of modulators of microgial activity, and possibly as therapeutic agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bioactive lipids, such as polyunsaturated fatty acids, are not mere inert molecules, but rather potent regulators of microglial function and hence brain health and disease.
bioactive fatty acids can be considered as a new class of modulators for the innate immunity of the brain.
the microglia are not only the brain’s first line of defense against pathogens and toxins, but they are also the main players in the brain’s ability to adapt to its environment, including diet.
